column4: Conventions: 'the base' is docs/ARCHITECTURE.md with amendments c, d, e folded in and file g items 102-110 as the coherence pass applies them; a § points into the base, 'V08 §' into this volume; SettlementForge field names and values quoted freely (owner's own project; amendments d, gate 2); no SF code excerpted; nothing from SF's map programs or map designs used; BCR-V8-n (§10), J-V8.n (§9), T-V8-n (§7).

Plain words: SF gets a Map tab on every settlement page; first opened by someone with GM rights, the map is drawn from the dossier (every listed institution sited sensibly, population fills the right number of houses, walls, gates, harbour and quarters match; everything unsaid derived by the map's rules from the same seed); the map never writes back into the dossier. On change (DM event, decree, week, season, year) the map compares the new dossier with facts it carries, works out what changed, reads each change's week from the dossier's receipts, changes the town as little as it can; history panel says what moved and why in SF's words ('bankrupt', 'destroyed by disaster'); after the DM advances time campaign maps catch up one by one in the background; a map opened before its turn catches up at once.

Plain words: custom institutions and chains from SF's homebrew library arrive like built-in ones; the map reads scene type, category and tags and (when handed over) the fuller library entry; an active supply chain laid out as one working line (raw material at its field or quarry, workshops stepping inward, seller near the market); renaming a custom item changes nothing; revising moves it only as far as needed. 'Blacksmiths (3-10)' drawn as several smithies, a guild as its hall with workshops, a 'district' as a quarter, never twice when SF lists the smaller form; SF supply chains tie mills, bakeries, markets together, a weakened chain pulls less; a coastal town whose record names a war or hostile sea partner walls its quays; a storm leaves damage where it struck; ancient ruins, magical node, ley lines or a magical past put an older town's ruins beneath; mines and mountains make caverns likelier; catacombs only under cemeteries, never under churches, only from a town upward; the cathedral always has the largest crypt; a cemetery the record closes stops its catacomb growing; nothing lost below.

Plain words: in a city (10 000 people or more) whose record lists its water system the map may carry an aqueduct on arches from a spring or river in reach to the city's conduit house, and a raised road may link a citadel, palace or cathedral on high ground; a town gets these only if the DM draws them; they are the map's own additions, removable by the DM and staying removed through later updates; the history panel says why each was built; a toll bridge gets a stream to cross, never a bridge over dry land.

Plain words: DM sees and edits everything, co-DM edits too; players never receive the DM's map file or SF's record: their Map tab shows pictures of the town as the party knows it (unlearned place drawn but not named), redrawn after every DM save and reveal ('Reveal to the party'; 'See what the players see' switch); gallery and public pictures show only public names, SF-veiled words veiled; SF's AI assistant reads the map, answers 'where is the tannery and why', proposes changes as ghosts the DM accepts or drops; a player's assistant reads only the party's known places.

Plain words: the map program runs in its own frame on its own web address (as SF's realm map does), none of its code beside SF's accounts or payments; each map stored by SF next to its settlement, never inside the dossier, as a saved file plus the list of changes since, 'with two older copies kept as backups'. An unreadable dossier, an unknown SF version, or a settlement shrunk below the town floor never breaks the map: it shows the last good town with a plain note ('This map is held as it was. The settlement's record could not be read.'), loses nothing, catches up when a readable dossier arrives; 'A settlement under 1 500 people waits for the village product, which will plug into the same doorway; when it exists, a town that shrinks into a village, or a village that grows into a town, keeps one map.' Map tab: saved picture at once, live map within about a second for a town and two for a large city; player's tab opens the party's pictures at once; nothing asks the DM to fill in a form; nothing in SF has to change to make a map.

Offer decision and coalescing: the host cannot compute the fact hash, so it compares raw dossiers: hashDossier = SHA-256 (Web Crypto) of canonical JSON (keys sorted by code point, no insignificant whitespace, numbers as JavaScript prints them), lower-case hex; the DM's or co-DM's client offers when hashDossier(dossier) != record.lastOffer.dossierHash or when the record is held (every new dossier is a retry), never otherwise; a player's page never offers; the port decides at the fact level (J-V8.4): differences only outside the carried facts (generation log, prose, simulationTrace, never-read keys) return unchanged and the host stores the new lastOffer with nothing appended (T-V8-6). Coalescing (J-V8.23): at most one offer in flight per session; a newer dossier replaces any queued one; when the in-flight result returns the newest is offered against the new head; the client counts skipped versions in its report field coalesced (client-side; no port note; C8-34); skipped versions lose nothing (the port diffs carried facts against the newest; each change's week from receipts, §4.11 (2)); an element appearing and vanishing between offers is never seen (same answer as SF's end-state).

Port leader: the port runs inside the module (generation worker, beside the document), never in SF's bundle (J-V8.1); only an editing role (DM owner or co-DM editor) holds the document, dossier and a port; a player holds neither (C8-01; J-V8.2 revised); digest, creation, absorb are pure functions of (document, dossier, HostContext, adapter and table versions), so every editing client computes the same events; every port event carries reserved session host:port (C8-15; BCR-V8-19) so events are byte-identical whichever editor computed them (T-V8-3) and no user's undo stack holds one. Creation (no map record): host mints mapId, sends dossier.offer {create {mapId}}; module runs digest -> creation (§14: blueprint, creation prefix, binding, carried facts) -> generate(blueprint, {docId: mapId, prefix}) (BCR-V8-2; J-V8.13); replies dossier.result {created, created: SnapshotBlock, factHash, report} (.plat bytes with logHead, lastSeq, outputVersion, schemaVersion, documentDigest computed by the module; C8-04); host calls MapStore.create as handed ('exists' -> another client won; reload the stored record, byte-identical by determinism, T-V8-3), writes the two thumbnails and renders the first party picture set. Absorb (a record exists): digest -> absorb(doc, digest, host) (§14; steps §3.5-§3.6), dry-run on the working state (§7.1; never refused by map locks or pins, applied around them, §7.7 items 2, 5), replies dossier.result {absorbed, baseLogHead, events, encoded, seqAfter, logHeadAfter, factHash, week, report} WITHOUT folding; host treats it as a doc.changed: if baseLogHead is current it commits (MapStore.commitEvents), sets its head to logHeadAfter, fans doc.apply out to every open session incl. the sender (which folds; §11.3 convergence); else doc.rejected {stale} and the module re-runs absorb on the new head (bounded: three attempts, then module.status {error} and a retry at the next offer). Verification by every editor (C8-37): an editing client folding a doc.apply with host:port events and holding the same dossier (last offer's hash equals the result's dossierHash) re-runs absorb on the pre-apply state and compares encodings; a difference is a port mismatch (module.status {error, detail host.verify.mismatch}, §3.9 B20, a report line naming the first differing event); never blocks the fold (T-V8-8). Two editors at once: both compute the same events; the host accepts the first, answers the second stale; the second's re-run finds nothing left (unchanged); no election protocol; the log's single head is the arbiter (J-V8.2).

Refresh queue (J-V8.6): after SF commits an advance, the host marks refreshPending on every map record whose dossier changed (hashDossier) and calls MapHost.refresh(queue) from the DM's page; the client creates ONE hidden frame (embed.html#p=2&mode=refresh: no tile worker, no view, no thumbnail pass until the end) processing the queue serially in campaign order, one document at a time: take the record's refresh lease (setStatus refreshing {by session, until now + 60 s}; refused when another live lease holds it; C8-30) -> doc.load + tail -> dossier.offer -> commit -> compact if the tail exceeds its threshold (§3.7) -> render the two thumbnails and party picture set (tile worker started for this step only) -> release lease with status current and refreshPending cleared -> close document, release memory -> next; lease renewed after each step, expires on its own (a dead page's lease expires within 60 s; record reads stale meanwhile). Scheduling: runs while the DM is not interacting with a map frame (paused on pointer or key input in any visible map session, resumes 5 s after the last), yields between maps, stops on AbortSignal. Page memory (C8-23): the refresh frame does not start while a visible map frame holds a CITY or METROPOLIS document; runs when the Map tab is closed or the visible document is a TOWN (at most one CITY or METROPOLIS document per page; §6 page row); queue persisted by refreshPending (next page resumes); a map opened in a visible tab while queued is absorbed there first and dropped from the queue; serial keeps memory at one rung's line (§12.8) plus the frame's fixed cost (a campaign of 20 CITY maps after a year in about 1.5 minutes of background work incl. party sets, §6).

Changes to events (1) Dating: each change reads its receipt row (§7.7 item 13): the first receipt present gives cause, fate and week by §4.11's rungs; HostContext.week the last rung; no rung -> week null and an unreceipted_change note; V08's kinds dated by rows F-V8-1..F-V8-7 of tables/dossier/receipts (BCR-V8-20): a relation by its powers' pulse week when stamped, else arrival; port-values by arrival riding the next epoch; a custom definition by arrival; a chain (custom or SF's) by arrival; a dependency by arrival; a calamity by its own tick (a receipt); the evidence singleton by arrival riding the next epoch. (2) Order: by week (null last), then decrees before other sources, then the dossier's own record order, then binding key. (3) Epochs by the cadence (§4.11 (4); C8-31; J-V8.55): from the last epoch's week W0 (its EpochRecord, else creation week) to the absorb's week W1 (latest dated week, else HostContext.week, else W0): an epoch at every calendar year end W with W mod 52 = 0 in (W0, W1] (sf445 calendar); an epoch at the first week the population leaves the last epoch's populationTarget ±5 % (from populationHistory; with none at W1 when outside), the reference moving to that epoch's target so every crossing adds its own epoch; an epoch at the week of each newly carried calamity no other epoch falls on; each epoch's populationTarget = population at its week (latest populationHistory at or before, else linear between W0's target and W1's population, rounded to a person); circumstances = the new digest's slices (trade, economy, powers, government, port): SF keeps no interior history (V52, V56), every catch-up epoch reads the end state, declared (J-V8.25). Calamities (DR-V8.6 = V06's DR-V6.1, the same row: V06 the reader, V08 the inputs): each newly carried calamity is one entry {week, kind 'calamity', calamity: CalamityRef} in EpochInputs.events of the epoch at its week, CalamityRef = {id: its key, name, type, severity, targets: use ids of resolved bound targets, deaths} (deaths for V04's burial growth; X3); its F5 targets' dossier events at the same week ride the same epoch's EpochInputs.dossier so V06's hazard phase strikes them in place; an unjoined target dropped, noted calamity_unplaced; the calamity-to-hazard mapping is V06's table (J-V6.70).

(4) Ledger event (J-V8.14; C8-12, C8-13): the absorb's first event is one dossierFacts {changes, quarantined, notes, notesCleared} (BCR-V8-6): every DossierChange with full before and after carried facts and the WHOLE quarantine list after this absorb, author host, no model effect; folding sets carried[key] = after per change, DossierBinding.quarantined to the list, appends {seq, week W1, factHash, changeIds} to absorbed and removes changeIds older than the newest 64 (the dossier block rebuilt from the log by folding these events alone, equal to the stored block at every seq, §2.9); creation's prefix opens with the same event, every fact an add. Port's notes (SS-44; J-V8.98): notes holds in order this run's event-class notes and those standing notes whose identity DossierBinding.notes does not hold; notesCleared the identities of standing notes this run no longer writes; report-class notes never enter the log; folding sets DossierBinding.notes to the old list less notesCleared plus the standing notes of notes, identity order; no model rule reads either. custom_resolved and low_confidence notes of custom records added or revised are written after the dry run's fold and appended to notes before encoding (dry run's result stands; every editor's re-run computes the same bytes); they are event notes (live resolution is the why card's, V10 WhyAnswer.profile, V9 §2.7 chips). Every unmapped_kind note (standing) likewise written after the fold (dry run's at absorb, generate's at creation, loaded state for unchanged), its class the class building the record there (SR4-07; J-V8.112), before notes and notesCleared are computed, so a note whose built class changed at a rung change is cleared and written anew at the next port run. An unchanged digest writes no event; its notes reach the host's report only.

(5) Emission by receipt row response: assign -> assign of a dossier-backed assignment (§7.7 One path: S10b's dossier request, least-disruption order; at a rung of a product declaring a records placement that placement first, V6 §2.1 ProductDeclEpoch.records, V07 §3.12; SR5-06); unassign -> unassign; status -> setAttr of the assignment's state (and memberState for a collective by DR25); setAttr -> setAttr of the named path (re-designation mutates by §4.7 S11); rebind -> setAttr of the bound entity's dossier ref to the new key (fold re-points the binding row; no address changes, §6.3; BCR-V8-8), also for a ladder promotion, a relation re-keyed with its power and a notable re-bound after a reroll; a staged record -> dossierRecord (stressors' overlays among them); a count change -> assign of added members as dispersed additions or setAttr of memberState removed on the members DR25 picks (siting keyed by the assignment and the event's seq); epoch and every slice-level change (port-values, a chain, a dependency, the evidence singleton) -> the epoch of (3); a calamity -> (3)'s event; none -> nothing beyond the ledger; each emitted event carries its DossierChange in EditBase.dossierChange and the binding key in EditBase.dossier (§7.1). (6) Placement in the log; the session: element events fold as standalone events at their week between the epochs of (3); one dated exactly at an epoch's week rides that epoch's EpochInputs.dossier (§7.7 item 6); undated ones follow the last epoch, applied finished (no Works); all take seq from nextSeq in this order, author host, reserved session host:port, never a user's session, no group (C8-15; BCR-V8-19); envelope session the same (§11.3 Logging).

Refusals at absorb: a digest whose population routes outside the base ladder with no registered product (§3.10) refuses the whole absorb (§7.7 item 15), as does E_OTHER_SETTLEMENT; nothing emitted, map held (§3.9). Deserted settlement (SS-21): with the village product registered, a population of 0 at an ABSORB routes to THORP and V07's desertion (V07 §2.1, §3.12; an outcome, never a refusal): a village-product document runs it at the epoch directly, a base-product document reaches it through V07 §2.1's fold, 0 below the band's lower edge (J-V8.85); at a CREATION population 0 refused E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE naming the floor (V07 §2.1); with no village product registered 0 is held like any population below 1 500 (B7).

Persistence (C8-04; J-V8.46): every encoded event, seq, head and snapshot field the store holds arrives in a message (doc.changed and dossier.result carry encoded, seqAfter, logHeadAfter; dossier.result.created and doc.snapshot.ready carry the whole SnapshotBlock); the host verifies only that a proposal's baseLogHead equals its head, stores the rest as handed, never decodes a byte, hashes an event or computes a head (T-V8-5 against a store that cannot). Commit: every committed event (user edit, absorb events, undo) appended via MapStore.commitEvents; stale -> doc.rejected {stale} (§11.3); an absorb's commit also writes absorbed and lastOffer in the same compare-and-set. Compaction (J-V8.5; C8-05, C8-29): when the tail passes 256 events or 256 KB, and at every created, upgrade and rebase, the committing editing client sends doc.snapshot and calls MapStore.replaceSnapshot with the reply's SnapshotBlock; precondition: snapshot logHead is the record's head or the logHeadAfter of an event in its tail (an edit committed meanwhile does not refuse it); the store keeps the tail's suffix, moves the old snapshot to backups[0] with the removed segment as tailAfter (C8-27), keeps backups[1] without its segment, drops older ones, one transaction; a snapshot whose head is in neither place is stale (restore or new map replaced the log) and discarded, the next commit's threshold check retries; the snapshot's canonical bytes include the whole log (§2.9) so nothing is lost; doc.snapshot is an editing role's message, not an export (E_HOST_FORMAT n/a). Load: snapshot plus tail replays exactly (T-V8-5).

Thumbnails: after each committed absorb and each compaction the committing client (or refresh queue) requests two 512-px PNGs — public key (anonymous and gallery fallback; exportPicture knowledge {tier public, places []}, J-V8.92) and secret (DM's; no knowledge) — at the city band with the document's style and a fixed sun (§11.1), stored with putThumbnails; shown before the frame is ready and after a failed boot; players' pictures are §3.14's party set. Backups and restore (J-V8.44; C8-28): backups hold the two previous snapshots; 'restore previous map' (§4.2) refuses a backup whose docId differs from mapId; else makes backups[0] the snapshot with an empty tail (swapped-out snapshot becoming backups[0]), then every open session gets a fresh doc.load (module.status {loading} between); the next offer absorbs the current dossier forward (dossier stays the truth; only the map's own edits since that snapshot lost; the dialog lists them). Local draft mirror (V09's; C8-35): in host mode only a draft mirror in the module origin's storage keyed by document id (V09 §3.8 (6)): unsent edits of a session, replayed at load only when its base head is the record's head or an event's logHeadAfter in the loaded tail, else discarded with 'unsaved changes from an earlier version of this map were dropped'; the mirror persists inside SF's page only when the module origin is same-site with SF's app ('Q1's recommendation (a subdomain of SettlementForge's own domain) meets it'); on another site it lives for the session only. Sizes (host quota per map): snapshot within §2.9's budget (TOWN <= 0.6 MB, CITY <= 3 MB, METROPOLIS <= 8 MB), tail <= 256 KB between compactions, two backups (newer with one tail segment <= 256 KB), two thumbnails <= 150 KB each, party set (§6: <= 2, 6, 12 MB); at CITY <= 15.9 MB worst case, typically about 8 MB.

Versions (ours): output version (§6.4): a stored document inside the retention window replays exactly under its own version; the owner's client gets module.status {upgrade-available} and the upgrade dialog with §7.5's diff; an accepted upgrade is an ordinary event over the bridge, compacted at once; players' pictures keep the stored version's drawing until the DM upgrades (J-V8.22); the owner's 'Update the map engine' action (§4.2) is the host's upgrade request V06 names for a document whose epochs carried dossier events (V6 §3.15), never upgraded by anything else; outside the window the document opens as §2.9's frozen view for everyone, the owner offered frozenImport rebase by V9 §3.14 (b)'s 'Edit it with this version', committed through doc.changed, then the client sends doc.snapshot (XV-V9-24); schema version: a newer document opens read-only (§2.9 step 1), an older module serving a newer document is a deployment error reported in module.status {error}; dossier row sets: absorb reads tables/dossier/* at the DOCUMENT's pinned versions (§2.9 tablePins), a new table version reaches a document only through upgrade. SF's side: a dossier carries schemaVersion, simulationVersion, generatorVersion; the same seed gives different dossiers on two lines at one generatorVersion, so the LINE names an adapter; the port never re-generates a dossier or reads SF code; SF's internal migrations reach the map only as a changed dossier shape.

New adapter version on the same line: at the next absorb, when binding.adapter.version differs from the running adapter's, the port first RE-BASELINES: per carried key, a difference confined to fields the new manifest's remaps list for that fromVersion is recorded in the ledger event with cause {kind adapter_remap} and response none (no map event), noted adapter_remap; every other difference is a real change absorbed as usual (J-V8.10); an adapter version changing a field's meaning without listing it fails T-V8-10 on the re-cut fixtures. New SF line (§14 item 1): one new adapter folder with its manifest; fixtures re-cut by the same scripts; fromLines declares how an older line's binding keys map (identity when the key law is unchanged); a document bound to line A receiving a dossier the registry gives to line B: B's fromLines entry for A re-keys the binding rows (a rebind setAttr per changed key, no address changes), binding.adapter becomes B's, line_migrated noted, absorb proceeds by the re-baseline with B's remaps for A; no fromLines entry for A -> E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED, held (J-V8.11). Release of a line: §8.3's checklist runs creation and absorb bars on the new line's fixtures, the cross-line migration on the old line's pairs, T-V8-10 and T-V8-11.

Failure handling (no failure discards or re-rolls a stored map, §5): a held map shows its last committed state with host.status.held and its reason row (the refusal's held note msg, a host.held.* row, stored as MapRecord.held.reason), status held, every later dossier a retry; words written once (host.held.*, host.recovered.*, host.verify.* here; host.status.*, host.party.* in §5.1; host.note.* in §4.6; SS-44); a refusal at CREATION shows host.status.notCreated and the reason row in the thumbnail slot; E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE's row by case: .village below the floor with no village product registered, .cap above 120 000 ({cap}), .empty a creation at population 0. Rows: B1 frame does not start (no ready within 20 s): re-create once -> stored thumbnail with retry; host.status.failed. B2 no reply (replyTimeoutMs): re-create frame and re-load -> thumbnail on second miss; host.status.stopped. B3 too big, too deep or not the line's shape (§3.5 steps 2-3): refuse E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE -> held; host.held.E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE 'The settlement's record could not be read.' (size_limit note in the host's report). B4 one malformed record (step 4): quarantine, absorb the rest; quarantined element keeps its last carried state (at creation not placed), retried every offer; host.note.quarantined_record. B5 no registered adapter accepts or the named line refuses (select): E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED naming candidates -> held (several accepting = B19); host.held.E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED 'This SettlementForge version is not supported by the map yet.' B6 another settlement's dossier: E_OTHER_SETTLEMENT -> held (catches a host bug); 'This record belongs to another settlement.' B7 population leaves the base ladder with no product (router §3.10): E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE naming village product or cap -> held (creation: no map, thumbnail slot says why); with the village product registered 0 at an absorb routes to THORP and V07's desertion, at creation 0 refused naming the floor (V07 §2.1; §3.6 (7); SS-21); texts .village 'Villages are drawn by the village map, which is coming later.', .cap 'Settlements of more than {cap} people are larger than the map draws.', .empty 'The settlement's record lists no inhabitants.' B8 head moved under an absorb (doc.rejected stale): re-run absorb three times -> module.status {error}, retried next offer; nothing or host.status.absorbing. B9 store compare-and-set fails: reload, re-apply as B8.

Failure rows cont.: B10 snapshot damaged or root mismatch (§2.9 step 3): §2.9's corrupt-cache replay from recipe and log -> if undecodable, backups[0] plus its tailAfter segment plus the current tail (exact) -> backups[1] absorbing forward, map edits since it lost and listed -> a new map from the current dossier, reported; module.status.detail beside ready: rungs 1-2 host.recovered.rebuilt 'The saved copy was damaged and has been rebuilt.'; rung 3 host.recovered.lost 'The saved copy was damaged and rebuilt from an older one; {n} of the map's changes were lost.' (lost edits listed in the report, V9 §5.7); rung 4 as B11. B11 map record gone (the host detects a mapId its store no longer holds; else it simply has none and makes one): a NEW map from the current dossier under a new mapId, one creation of the current state (§7.7 One path; item 22 (c) allows it to differ); old layout not recoverable (J-V8.43); host.recovered.newMap 'The saved map was lost, so a new one was made from the settlement's current record.' B12 absorb over its disruption budget (draft reroll, J-M11; §7.7 item 5 dry run): least-disruptive sites, reported over budget; the disruption report. B13 host restored an earlier dossier (factHash equals an earlier absorbed entry): F22 forward convergence (§7.7 item 5); host.note.state_matches_absorbed with the residue. B14 upgrade cannot copy a pack (§7.5 cap): keep the old model; upgrade dialog's message. B15 settlement deleted in SF: host deletes the map record; nothing in the module. B16 hostile string in a name: never executed (text rendering; every export escapes, §11.1 inert bar). B17 quarantined record whose key cannot be formed: every carried institution key absent from the new digest held (no remove), quarantine_hold, until readable (C8-12). B18 party pictures missing or older than the map: the viewer shows what is stored captioned with its week; the next editing session or refresh sends party.render (new set or unchanged); host.party.notOpened or host.party.asOf. B19 two adapters accept a new settlement's dossier, no line named: newest registered line, recorded, line_defaulted. B20 an editor's re-run differs (§3.3 verification): the applied log stands, mismatch reported with the first differing event (C8-37); module.status.detail beside error, editors only: host.verify.mismatch 'A map update did not match when it was checked; it has been reported.'

Village-tier hand-off: LadderRouter.route(population) (§1.1) is the one decision of which product builds a population; the village product registers its ProductDecl in StrategyRegistry.products (V07 §2.1; BCR-V7-11), the one registration of file f item 202; the port registers nothing and consults LadderRouter: at creation which product and rung build the population, at every absorb only whether the population lies in a registered range (SS-19, SS-28); the product's rungs, range, stages, strategies are V07's (not restated). With no village product registered, a population below 1 500 is refused (§7.7 item 15) and a mapped town shrinking below 1 500 is held at its last state (B7) until the population returns above 1 500 (then the next absorb diffs everything since in one pass). With it registered: a village-sized dossier is created on the village rung rows (V07 §3.11); a crossing is §4.11's rung change as BCR-V7-26 states it (the product at an epoch is V07 §2.1's fold with handoff.band: town to village and village to base only when an epoch's target leaves the band; inside it the previous product runs on its own rung row; SS-20); everything the epoch builds follows that product's stages; standing fabric survives (§6.3); population 0 at an absorb is V07's desertion (SS-21); one document, one seed, one history across both products (J-V8.12); V07 owns what the village builds and its fold; V08 owns the port's consultation and the one-document rule, tested by T-V8-19 with a test ProductDecl.

Staged records from the digest: Conditions and stressors (C8-09, C8-10 (c)): each digest condition put as a ConditionOverlay (cond:<id>; archetype, severity, sinceWeek, untilWeek) whatever its status (stable, worsening, easing; only live conditions listed); weeks from ticks: W = HostContext.week, else the latest tick of populationHistory, else 0 at creation; sinceWeek = round(W − duration.elapsedTicks); untilWeek = round(W + duration.expiresAtTicks − duration.elapsedTicks) (reading expiresAtTicks as the whole length; PLAUSIBLE: a generated condition carries elapsedTicks 3.25, expiresAtTicks 6 at tick 0); measurement: untilWeek within ±1 week across town-1's and city-1's one-week, one-season, one-year ticks (T-V8-18); pre-decided fallback if it drifts: untilWeek = expiresAtTicks read as an absolute tick; a condition no longer listed retired at the absorb's week; each stressor put under cond:stress:<type> (archetype its type, severity 0.5, sinceWeek its first absorb's week, no untilWeek), retired when no longer listed; effects by the conditions row (tint via §8.2's thematic rows, Works factors via DR21, activity scalars and dials at the next epoch); stressors add no EpochInputs.events entry (one path: the overlay; J-V8.56). Deposits (C8-18): each listed deposit put as a DepositSite (res:<key>; family by the deposits row, state); derived fields S12a's: reading the prefix's deposit puts ahead (BCR-V8-22) S12a draws the bearing on hinterland.outside keyed by the deposit key (realm block's bearing wins when given), writes bearingCdeg; the land use writes landUse (both derived, recomputed on regeneration, never in the event; DR19); a state change is a put at its week, converting the land use at the next epoch (§4.11); magical_node and ancient_ruins sites follow the deposits row and V04's ruinCentre(); a derived site res:derived:<landuse> by the same row (SR2-04).

Staged records cont.: Power relations (C8-10 (a)): each unordered pair put as a PowerRelation with the relations row's neutral kind, sign, strength x trend factor and hidden flag (BCR-V8-26 adds sign and hidden); §4.5's typing reads the prefix's relation puts ahead (BCR-V8-22) as a soft adjacency row (attraction positive, repulsion negative); item 72's political component reads them; a hidden relation never named on a public view (DR20). Notables: each put as a dossier-backed Person (npc:<id>) pinned whole, Posting at workplaceKey's element, Membership in powerKey's power, housed by §2.7's rule in the district of its institution or its power's seat (names joining nothing: governing power's seat district, noted name_unjoined); a successor (replaced names a carried notable) put with the old person's house and posting, old record retired (F17); dead or gone retired, the house stays a house; a reroll (C8-39; J-M11; F21's receipt): a vanished npc: key whose name and role equal a new key's is re-bound (rebind, noted npc_rebound) keeping house and posting; other vanished keys retired, the new put. History: at creation only Recipe.history = {ageYears: history.age, scars} (one scar per event by historyScars with yearsAgo and severity); never updated (ageYears never advanced by the host's weeks, §2.7); magical events to ruin evidence. Per-settlement values: PortValues (crime by crime row, importPct = foodImportPct / 100, foodChain = foodChains, legitimacy, threats by threats row, latitudeDeg null in the creation slice where Intent.latitudeDeg holds DR-V8.1's value; a later realm latitude fills it) in the creation slice and each epoch's slice.

Custom kinds (C8-17): the dossier's custom definitions are PortRows.customKinds rows DERIVED at read time: the table's rows (empty in the base) overlaid by one row per carried custom institution (kind = its definition id; no fallbackClass: the class is item 104 (a)'s resolution at fold, BCR-V11-26, J-VI.20; SS-37), and only from its carried custom-def fact (admitted library entry): economicWeight and criticality by the customWeights row (a dossier row set, not calibratable; J-V8.108), defenseRoles and powerAuthorities (the entry's defenseRole and authority) (BCR-V8-29); nothing written into the recipe's params (a revision changes them through its own setAttr's fold, no editTable, avoiding item 22's reshuffle). Realm block (J-V8.27; C8-21; BCR-V8-24): the client's realmBlockFrom(placements) computes host-side without module code from the campaign's placements (the settlement's and partners' realm positions), realm map scale and latitude scale, and the campaign's spatial digest (cell terrain, river, coast words) — nothing else of campaign state: each partner's bearingCdeg = round(100 x atan2(dx, −dy) in degrees) mod 36 000 (realm y grows southward), distanceM = hypot(dx, dy) x mPerRealmUnit, the cell, latDeg = degAtY0 − y x degPerUnitY when the latitude scale is given; used as §7.7 layer 2 states (true bearings, north first) and as DR-V8.1's first input; sent with an offer only when the settlement is placed on the realm. Audience in use: the client maps SF audience words via §14's table: DM's page mounts with dm (owner, secret), co-DM's with co-dm (editor, secret); a player's page never mounts a frame (party set and party gazetteer); anonymous, gallery and DM-full shares get picture exports only (§5.3); module takes the lower of told role and audience word (J-V8.29). Display names (J-V8.28): for a public picture the host computes with its own public-projection filter the veiled text of every name to veil and passes displayNames (binding key -> text) with that one export request; the module draws them for that export only (§11.1; T85-3 via the bridge, T-V8-16).

Determinism: the port reads no clock and no randomness beyond named streams: partner and deposit bearings on gate.pick and hinterland.outside keyed by the element's key; member choices on siting keyed by the assignment and the event's seq (§6.1); hashDossier's canonical JSON, the one-way seed, host-minted docId, reserved session host:port and pinned tables make creation and absorb byte-identical on every editing client and engine (T-V8-3, T73-8), letting two editors race safely and every editor verify an applied absorb (C8-37); epoch weeks and population targets are integer arithmetic on receipts; a condition's weeks rounded to the nearest week; party pictures drawn from the committed document under a fixed key, style and sun (two renders of one head give byte-identical tiles; T-V8-41).

Custom content arrival (item 104's host side; the map's use of it is item 104's base mechanism with V11's rows; runs inside digest after step 6, pure): (1) record: for each source 'custom' institution: custom.uid = localUid; definitionId, revision, contentHash from the record's own fields else from the materializedDefinitions row of the same localUid; with neither contentHash = H128 over canonical CBOR of (name, category text, tags, scene tokens) and a custom_unversioned note (an edit of those fields still reads as a revision); categoryText trimmed; group by the categories chain; required from required; a record without localUid keys by name (§7.7 item 12's third rung), noted custom_unkeyed. (2) scene tokens sceneProfileId, landmarkLevel, materialFamily checked against the adapter's copy of the line's enumerations (17, 2, 6 values); unknown dropped, noted unmapped_word; absent stay absent. (3) keywords (item 104 (a)(6)): name then description: Unicode NFKC, lower-cased, split on every non-letter non-digit, tokens < 3 characters dropped; each token and each adjacent pair joined by one space looked up in keywords; matches kept in order of first occurrence up to 16, then sorted; the description read here and nowhere else (not carried, not in the digest, never in the document; §7.7 item 1 prose rule; J-V8.32); SF advises reading tags before names so keys enter as the weakest rung and the report marks a profile decided by them low_confidence. (4) resources: each config.nearbyResourceDefinitions[] entry with custom true -> customResources under res:uid:<localUid>, also listed in site.deposits with custom true and state available (DR19, DepositSite); family and land use from the admitted library's resource category (water -> river or coast; land -> fields or pasture; subterranean -> a mine or quarry at the hinterland edge; special -> its own deposit site; item 104 (b)), else from its name's keywords, else land. (5) services: each availableServices.<category>[] entry with custom true -> customServices under svc:uid:<localUid>, serviceCategory = bucket, provider = binding key of the institution its institution name joins (exact, then the line's slug); no join -> absent, noted custom_node_unjoined.

Custom content arrival cont.: (6) chains: each economicState.customChains[] -> customChains under chain:<chainId>: active = activation.state active and status active (the dossier's verdict; J-V8.33); resource name joined to a custom resource (exact, then slug), else to a catalogue deposit by the deposits table's label; processors joined to institutions' keys in listed order; each output's uid from the tradeEndpointOwners.exports[] entry whose label equals it; exports, imports, promoted as given; an unjoined node keeps its name, noted custom_node_unjoined (the chain still pulls between joined nodes). (7) cross-links and volume: from admitted library entries only: each requires, produces, requiredInstitution, requiredResources reference of a chain node (custom:<localUid> to that item's key; prebuilt:<category>:<slug> to inst:cat:<slug> when the roster holds that key, else to the institution whose slugged name equals <slug>) becomes a crossLinks row (item 104 (h)(4)); unresolved noted name_unjoined and dropped; volume = the last processor's admitted economicWeight, else moderate (item 104 (h)(2)). (8) library (item 104 (a)(5); J-V8.31): an entry of HostContext.customLibrary ADMITTED only when definitionId, revision and contentHash equal a definition the dossier materialised; others ignored with one library_mismatch note (the library can enrich, never add; item 20 (h)); admitted -> customDefs, carried as custom-def facts under def:<definitionId>; an offer WITHOUT a library changes nothing carried (def: keys diffed only when the new digest holds them); a definition whose revision changes with no admitted entry for the new revision: old def: fact removed (response none; custom_library_dropped); resolution falls back to the dossier's rungs until the host sends the new entry. (9) creation prefix order: after the dossierFacts ledger event, dossierRecord puts (conditions, catalogue deposits, custom resources, power relations, custom chains in key order, custom services); then assigns (first the institution nodes of every ACTIVE chain, chains in key order, nodes in flow order, a node in two chains at first appearance, so downstream after suppliers; item 104 (h)(4); J-V8.41); then every other record in dossier order; then notables' Person puts; absorb emits in §3.6's order, within one week chain records before their nodes' assigns, upstream first. (10) changes: new custom record = add (F1); new contentHash = attr cause custom_revision emitted as setAttr of the assignment's custom.revision (fold re-resolves and re-sites by item 22's least disruption; item 104 (e)); a chain becoming active = CustomChainRecord put active true at its arrival week (nodes re-sited against each other by least disruption upstream first; item 104 (h)(7)); becoming inactive = put active false (nodes keep sites, lose pulls); a chain no longer listed retired, one returning under the same chainId put again on its retired record (nodes never moved; item 104 (h)(8) toggle bar); a service whose provider changes = put with the new provider. (11) never fails (item 104 (d)): malformed custom record quarantined as any record; unknown words, unjoined nodes, mismatched library entries are notes; counts join maxRecords (200 per list). Determinism: pure function of dossier, admitted library entries and pinned tables (archetypes, categorySynonyms, keywords, categories, tags, deposits); admitted fields carried in the document so replay never needs the host (§11.4).

Players' view (C8-01, C8-14, C8-36; J-V8.57): a player never holds the map (§11.1 Knowledge: a host keeping a place secret sends pictures and interchange exports, never the document; SF builds its player face from a public projection, CONFIRMED at 5d699cc68); the players' tab is fed from the map record alone (stored pictures and a stored list of words made by an editing session or refresh frame under the party's key). (1) Party key: MapRecord.party (base tier public or local and places revealed above it: binding keys for dossier elements, addresses for map places); rendering resolves it to BCR-V10-22's key form {tier, places} (the Admission form of §2.9's view-state knowledge), places always present, each binding key through the binding rows to its entity's address (a collective to all its members), each address as given; a key no longer resolving skipped but kept (a re-opening re-reveals it); every party render passes that key as ExportOpts.knowledge (BCR-V9-14) and as admitAs of each query (BCR-V10-22), admitting what both the session's secret key and the party key admit (BCR-V8-27; SR2-06); the module never raises a key. (2) Set: (a) PNG tile pyramid, 256-px tiles, row-major, z0 city band, z1 district, z2 neighbourhood over the frame of the document's city-band view, plus a z3 building-band level ONLY for tiles covering an admitted place above public (each place's bounding box plus 40 m), capped at 64 tiles; (b) the city-band SVG under the same key, inert by §11.1 (text as outlines, no script, no external reference), offered for printing; (c) the party gazetteer: answers of query(h, {kind gazetteer or people, ...}, {admitAs the party key}) (band-less, admitted as at the city band, §11.2; every page carrying that admitAs, SR2-07), paged to one JSON document projected through §5.4 (3)'s words-only rows (names, kinds, districts, tiers, dossier reasons, no coordinates) before storage; what a player's assistant reads (§4.4 (1)); every picture drawn with the document's style, fixed sun, public notes, view pins and annotation layer (§2.9, §9.5), never a private note or DM-only pin (C8-36).

Players' view (3) When made and bridge crossing (J-V8.91): the client of an editing session sends party.render {party, since?} (a) after each absorb it commits, (b) 30 s after the last map edit batch it committed (debounce restarts at each commit; a closing session with a pending render sends it first and waits), (c) at once after each setParty, (d) at creation; the refresh queue sends it for every map it refreshes; on every open the client checks the stored set against the record (absent, or logHead, partyRev or outputVersion differing; B18) and sends at once on a difference; the module resolves the party, builds the levels' display lists, SVG and gazetteer, computes drawDigest; when since holds the same partyRev, outputVersion and drawDigest it answers unchanged without rasterising (no store write); else rasterises in the tile worker between edit batches (never delaying an edit; §12.6 settle rule) and answers rendered with seqAt and logHead = the head drawn and partyRev = the request's party.rev; the client stores it via putPartyPictures (keeps the newer by integer pair (seqAt, partyRev); 'older' returned, nothing written), then re-sends host.state {partyPicturesAt}. (4) Player's tab: mountParty reads the record and shows the set in the small viewer (PartyView; <= 4 KB gzipped of the client's budget; no model code): grid of img tiles under a CSS transform, wheel, pinch and arrow keys, a level switch at each band's scale, caption host.party.asOf (set's week), a focusable region labelled host.party.region; with no set, the public thumbnail and host.party.notOpened; holds no frame, module, dossier or session, sends no message (T-V8-17); refreshFromStore re-reads when the host learns the set changed (its own subscription; no push). (5) DM's check (SR-05; J-V8.87): 'See what the players see' (header toggle or seePlayersView(on) posting host.state {playersView}) sets ViewOpts.viewAs to the party key {tier, places} (BCR-V9-23 per SR-06): a display filter under which the frame draws, labels and reads what both its key and the party key admit (V9 §2.10 effectiveKey(); SR2-09); off clears viewAs; while on the View as menu reads 'What the players know' (V9 §4.8, J-V9.85); the frame's key stays secret (J-V9.46) so document formats, doc.snapshot, compaction, draft mirror keep working; a new party or an absorb changing binding rows re-resolves the filter; no view state, store write or event; strip 'Showing what the players see' in the banner slot. (6) Replaces SF's retired map rows' fog table and audience-tagged annotations (research s E-7, §3): area fog consciously replaced by place-by-place knowledge (J-V8.58; §9.2); a revealed place named in every picture from then on; 'an area fog over a live map is the "party copy" capability of owner question Q5, not built'.

No new authoring tool: a DM edits an SF map with item 101's twelve tools exactly as a standalone map (§7.1, §14) under §7.7's precedence line; every map edit (move, lock, rejected site, positive placement, style) lives in the map's log and survives every absorb (§7.7 items 3-5). The two added event kinds dossierFacts and dossierRecord (BCR-V8-6) are host-authored: an edit of either kind whose author is not host or session not host:port, or arriving in a doc.changed from a client, is refused F-EDIT dossier-owned (§5.2, §7.7 item 11); only an editing client's dossier.result produces them; a user's edit of a staged record's fields (a condition's severity, a notable's posting) refused the same way; its display (label text, visibility) stays the user's (§9.1). Generated item-110 content never dossier-bound (C8-42; J-V8.66; BCR-V8-31): a raised way, retaining wall (a generated terrace's walls among them) or deck plot the generator made is generated content (SR2-16: a terrace itself is a flatten stroke with its walls, so no delete targets it and file f item 260 has no suppression kind for it); carries no Identity.dossier even when a record fed its reason; provenance names that record for the clerk's why; removed by the base's delete of generated content (§7.1), never §7.7 item 3's rejectSite, so the removal never lapses; the conduit house bound to the water record stays dossier-backed (a map delete of it is a rejectSite); a TOWN aqueduct only by drawing (T4 road raised or aqueduct class), held as a declaration.

Host-side actions in the Map tab (each a frame header control offered by role, except the load-mismatch keep drawn by the shell; one event or store operation each with its undo and lifecycle; only owner and editor have a frame; SR-04; J-V8.88): a control whose operation is the page's posts host.action {action, args?} surfaced as MapSession.on('action') and the host runs the row's operation; a control committing an event ('Update the map engine') commits in the frame via doc.changed then asks for doc.snapshot; 'See what the players see' runs in the frame alone; keeping the saved town after a load mismatch has no header control (V9 §3.14's load-mismatch choice shown to the owner; one event one control, J-V8.94); confirmation dialogs ('Restore previous map', 'Make a new map from the record') in the frame first (restore dialog lists map edits after backups[0].logHead from host.state), posting only on confirmation; no control posts anything else (T-V8-47). Rows: Refresh now (owner, editor): host.action refresh -> offer current dossier -> committed dossier events; undo none (dossier events no undo target; converges if host restores, F22); lifecycle lastOffer, absorbed, party set re-rendered. Update the map engine (owner): upgrade to the running output version; dialog summarises §7.5's diff in words (what moves, what the new version adds incl. raised ways, retaining walls, deck plots each removable after, what it retires; C8-47 (3)); an upgrade event via doc.changed, then doc.snapshot and replaceSnapshot; undo of the upgrade (§7.5) in the session and after reload while from is in the window; snapshot.outputVersion changes at compaction; party set re-rendered. Keep the saved town (owner; after a load mismatch; no header control): §2.9 step 4's keep via V9 §3.14 (error.mismatch Keep saved / Use rebuilt, V9 §4.9); after the rebase commits, doc.snapshot; undo §7.4's rebase undo; §11.3's bridged rule: other clients install it. Restore previous map (owner): backups[0] the snapshot with an empty tail, then absorb the current dossier; refuses a foreign docId; host.action restore after the dialog -> replaceSnapshot with the backup; fresh doc.load to every open session; then an offer; undo 'restore' again swaps back (backups rotate); dialog lists edits lost incl. a removal of generated item-110 content made after the backup.

Host actions cont.: Make a new map from the record (owner): a fresh creation from the current dossier under a new mapId, old record kept under its own mapId; host.action newMap after the dialog -> creation offer under a new host-minted mapId and MapStore.create; the host points the settlement at it; fresh doc.load to every open session; undo 'Go back to the old map' (host points back) while the host keeps it; old mapId not deleted by the module; whether and how long the host keeps it is the host's (B11 detects a pointer to a lost one); old backups never mixed into the new one's. Reveal to the party (owner, editor): host.action reveal {places} -> setParty({reveal}) -> MapStore.setParty (CAS on party.rev), party set re-rendered, host.state {party} re-sent; undo 'Hide again' host.action hide {undo true} -> setParty({prev true}) (one step; an older reveal undone by hiding it). Hide from the party (owner, editor): host.action hide {places} -> setParty({hide}); undo 'Reveal again' host.action reveal {undo true} -> setParty({prev true}). The party's base knowledge (owner): party.tier public or local (a party native to the town); host.action partyTier {tier} -> setParty({tier}); undo partyTier {undo true} -> prev. See what the players see (owner, editor): the frame's ViewOpts.viewAs = party key, display filter, key stays secret (§3.14 (5); SR-05); header toggle or seePlayersView -> host.state {playersView}; no view-state write, store write, event or host.action; undo the same toggle; session memory only. Assistant settings (owner): chooses V10's configuration for the built-in clerk and its spending cap: host.action assistantSettings -> the host opens its own assistant settings (SF's settings surface outside the Map tab; J-V8.35 holds for the tab) and calls setClerk(config) -> V10's clerk.config (V10 §3.17; BCR-V10-7) -> ClerkMount.host and HostSlots.clerkMode; undo the previous configuration re-sent; the host keeps the choice, the module keeps no secret beyond the session.

Locality: a dossier event mutates only its disruption set (§7.7 item 5; T20-8) around every lock, pin, positive placement and declared entity (§7.2); an edit it can no longer honour is reported and orphaned, never dropped (J-A20.73); a DM's rejection of a dossier element's site holds until the settlement grows or declines past the roster tolerance (§7.7 item 3); nothing a player does changes the model (no document, no session); players' reveals change only MapRecord.party, never the log. Removal hold for generated item-110 content (C8-42 (2), (3)): removing a generated raised way, retaining wall (incl. a generated terrace's walls) or deck plot (§4.1; file f item 260's suppression kinds raised, retaining, deckPlot) holds through every absorb, catch-up epoch, rung change, line re-key (rebind, §3.8), upgrade (§7.5's mapping hands the tombstone to its successor), load-mismatch keep (V9 §3.14; rebase keeps the log's edits) and a host undo re-offering an older dossier (F22; the delete stays in the log); only 'Make a new map from the record' drops it, and 'Restore previous map' when the restored backup predates it (listed among lost edits); a removed raised way's slot stays closed: when a later dossier change raises the cap (§2.6b (1)(d)) the reason may open a NEW slot only, announced as new by the history panel (§4.6); the slot mechanism is item 110's in the base (routed to the coherence pass with critique-V5's same request for islands, X8).

Host clerk (SF's assistant as a §11.2 clerk; nothing added for it; §14; J-A101.83): (1) session, rights and relay (C8-01, C8-20; J-V8.73): acts only inside an editing user's session (DM or co-DM) via that session's MapSession.query and .preview with that user's role and key, never a role of its own (J-V8.21); wherever its model loop runs (SF's server or page; SF's assistant not surveyed), its map tools RESOLVE IN THE DM'S PAGE: the page receives the tool call via SF's own channel, executes it with query or preview and returns the answer the module posted, already projected in the frame (§5.4 (3); BCR-V10-7 (c)); no projection code in the page, never a full answer (SS-01); no map open -> the client opens a headless session (refresh mode's frame) for the call and closes it after (one load, §6); a player's assistant never has a session: it reads the stored party gazetteer on SF's side. (2) Reading: kinds offered are §5.4 (3)'s table (SS-04): base gazetteer, people, whereIs, relations, fates; V10 §3.17's reader kinds brief, entity, sites, why (with sections), frame without near and radiusM, rule, profile; measure, hit, inView refused E_HOST_KIND; answers paged at 64 KB, every row marked with its tier (dossier, declared, map) and filtered by the key; a dossier element's why names the derivation row that placed it (DR10), the relation, supply and siting rows that pulled it (item 103 families from provenance; V11's rows), the dossier change that caused its current state (changeId, source, week, SF's own reason; §7.7 item 13); 'why is this quarter poor' reads the field's drivers incl. item 102's daylight share (answer form V10's); for generated item-110 content why names its reason (drop, link, water need) and the DR-V8.7 or DR-V8.8 inputs read (C8-47 (4)).

Host clerk cont.: (3) Proposing: via MapSession.preview(events, {view true, proposal}) (BCR-V10-7 (b) body); what the frame does is V10 §3.17's host proposal intake (cited): card in the frame, Accept sends doc.changed with proposedBy 'clerk' and the DM as author, module's clerk.proposal {id, status, seqs?} reaches the page as clerkProposal; a refused clerk.config as clerkConfigRefused (SS-03); a proposal touching a dossier fact refused dossier-owned with closest alternatives (§7.7 item 11) (the assistant can suggest where the dossier's smithy stands, never add, remove or rename it); a proposal to remove generated item-110 content is an ordinary delete, never refused. (4) Prose: the map passes no dossier prose to any assistant (no description seed on this port line; V10 §1b.5; BCR-V10-14); SF's assistant has the dossier on its side (SS-05). (5) Limits: one preview in flight per session (a newer replaces a pending one; §12.6 settle rule); queries answered in the generation worker between batches, never delaying an edit. (6) The built-in clerk (V10) in host mode runs inside the module; the DM chooses its configuration via 'Assistant settings' (setClerk -> clerk.config -> bridge handler -> ClerkMount.host, HostSlots.clerkMode); the harness's needsToken() posts clerk.needsToken -> clerkNeedsToken; SF answers with a new short-lived token via setClerk (V10 §3.17); under V10's configuration B (prompt via SF's proxy) the map block and every tool result pass V08 §5.4 (3)'s words-only projection before leaving the frame; under A (provider called from the frame) nothing reaches SF; 'C (this section's own assistant, the default recommended) needs no built-in clerk'. Custom content under editing (§4.5): a DM's declarations about a custom kind (place, quarter, pin, siting-profile override; item 104 (a)(1)) name the element by inst:uid:<localUid>, surviving every rename and revision; a revision's re-siting is a dossier event moving around every lock, pin, positive placement (§7.7 item 5); CustomChainRecord and CustomServiceRecord dossier-owned: a user's or clerk's edit of their fields refused dossier-owned with map-side alternatives (placeAt a node, rejectSite); the clerk's why on a custom element names the resolution rung (declaration, archetype, category, tags, library field, keywords, fallback), the chain rows and the low_confidence mark.

DM's view of what the dossier did: every line a catalogue key with args (V9 §2.9 MsgRef); words written once (this section's tables, V10 §3.9, V06's chronicle templates, V9 §4.9's rows history.dossierFacts.creation, report.moved.<kind>, report.dossier.<state>; J-V9.109); panels render them, never compose (SS-43, SS-44; J-V8.99; SR2-24 (c)). Absorb group (V9 §4.10; C8-47 (1), (2)): each committed absorb (its dossierFacts ledger event and the port's host:port events after it up to the next ledger event or another session's event; §3.6 step 6; V9 §4.10 dossier groups J-V9.107; SR2-24 (d)) drawn as one group headed host.group.absorb ('{n} changes from SettlementForge, week {week}') or host.group.absorbUndated ('{n} changes from SettlementForge') when the week is null; {n} = DossierChange count; inside in order: (1) the changes (each dossier event as V9 §4.10's dossier-event row with its report entries by V9 §4.9's report.moved.<kind>); (2) the port's notes (one line per note of the ledger event's notes rendered by the table, Show when keys bind elements resolved by V9 §4.10's entity read by dossierKey, BCR-V9-36; a line binding an element the view's effective key does not admit not drawn; §11.2 Knowledge; SR-24); (3) what the absorb's epochs built by item 110 (each epoch V9 §4.10's epoch row, V06's chronicle, V6 §3.15.1: raised way founded, finished, repaired or run dry = chronicle's raisedWay entry, its 'Why here?' opens the raised section, row info.raised.built with DR-V8.7 or DR-V8.8 inputs as facts rows of tier dossier (V10 §3.9); a reason firing at a slot the DM closed = one line info.raised.suppressed ({w} the removal's week; V10 §3.9; CVR-V10-14) drawn as the epoch row's line from V06's EpochReport.raised.suppressedFired (V6 §2.10, filled by V6 §3.19.3 (2); XV-V9-28; J-V9.113; X21) with Show on the removal's former outline; a way founded in a slot a cap increase opened is an ordinary founding entry (slot rule J-VI.14); the panel recomputes nothing); creation's prefix listed the same way under V9 §4.10's creation row.

Standing notes (SS-44; SR-23, SR-24): the report panel reads report(h) (§5.4 GenerationReport); its dossier section (V9 §5.7) lists GenerationReport.dossier (placement state) then GenerationReport.dossierNotes under host.group.standing ('How the map reads SettlementForge's record'), one line per note, Show on its keys, a line the effective key does not admit not drawn; dossierNotes = DossierBinding.notes at the report's seq, copied by every derivation's report build (BCR-V8-8), so every frame and reload shows the same list; standing notes stay while each port run writes them and appear in an absorb group only in the absorb that first wrote them; report-class notes and every note of an offer answered unchanged or refused reach only the host's report (dossier.result.report, on('report')), rendered through statusText. Held state is no history row (a held absorb commits nothing): tab banner and frame's held notice show host.status.held with MapRecord.held.reason. Party group: reveals, hides, base-knowledge changes listed as the DM's own actions (host.revealed, host.hidden, host.partyTier) with host.picturesDrawn in the panel's group 'The party' via HostSlots.historyLines (V9 §4.10; SR2-01, SR2-03) made from successive host.state values (no reveal history beyond party.prev; J-V8.58); drawn by V9 §4.10's rule for host lines; undo §4.2's 'Hide again' or 'Reveal again' (SR3-06).

Port notes in words (SS-44; J-V8.97-99): one row per PortNote kind (the base's eight and §2.4's twenty-seven), key host.note.<kind> (held: §3.9's host.held.* rows); each one sentence of at most 25 words in V9 §4.9's style; args from msg.args (names as the dossier writes them, never an id); Show lists keys; class decides where kept (event: that run's ledger event, drawn in its absorb group; standing: the ledger event only when new, then DossierBinding.notes while every run writes it, drawn from GenerationReport.dossierNotes; report: the host's report only). Rows (kind: words; class): unmapped_kind '{name} is a kind the map does not know yet, so it is built like any {class}.' (class = the label cell (V11 §2.3, BCR-V9-8) of the class building it at the document's rung; at a village rung the class V07 §3.11 steps 2-4 give (villageForm, archetype village cell, or tag fallback, whose market entry names V11's market class); or a pin kind's host.pinKind.<kind> row; read after the fold) standing; unmapped_word standing; ignored_key report; unreceipted_change event; rename_without_receipt event; duplicate_key standing; state_matches_absorbed event; realm_block_used report; quarantined_record standing; quarantine_hold event; adapter_remap event; line_migrated event; line_defaulted event; held report; size_limit report; ladder_merged standing; ladder_promoted event; ladder_unknown standing; chain_node_unjoined standing; unmapped_good standing; npc_rebound event; calamity_unplaced event; custom_resolved '{name} is built like any {class} ({rung}).' (class as unmapped_kind's; at a village rung the archetype's village cell decides — a mercantile-market record names the market cross by host.pinKind.market_cross; rung V9 §2.7 chips words) event; custom_unversioned standing; custom_node_unjoined standing; library_mismatch event; custom_library_dropped event; low_confidence event; uncatalogued_step standing; derived_landuse standing; name_unjoined standing; name_ambiguous standing; custom_unkeyed standing; count_over_range standing; not_placed standing. Pin kinds' words (SR6-06): host.pinKind.shrine 'wayside shrine', host.pinKind.well 'well', host.pinKind.market_cross 'market cross', loaded by V11's registry row 87 with V08's other host.* rows; legend symbol-key words are the base's and application's (§9.5; V09). Group heads host.group.absorb, host.group.absorbUndated, host.group.standing. T-V8-14's walker fails the build on a PortNote kind or PortRefusalCode case without its row, a row over 25 words, or an arg a row names that its note does not fill.

SF's side draws three things only (J-V8.35): the tab's container, the stored thumbnail as an img until the frame's first live frame, and a one-line status banner driven by module.status (plus on a player's tab the client's party viewer, part of the client); banner words have ONE source, V09's host.* catalogue rows generated into statusText defaults at build (C8-40; the host may translate); keyed by phase: booting, loading, verifying -> host.status.opening 'Opening the map...' with progress (owner, editor); absorbing -> host.status.absorbing 'Catching up with the settlement's record...' (owner, editor); held -> host.status.held 'This map is held as it was.' followed by the reason row MapRecord.held.reason (owner, editor); upgrade-available -> host.status.upgrade 'A newer map engine is available — use Update in the map's header' (no button; SR2-04) (owner); error -> host.status.stopped 'The map stopped; reopening it.', then host.status.failed 'The map could not start.' with Retry (owner, editor); any phase with detail -> the host.* row detail names beside the phase's row (B10 host.recovered.*, B20 host.verify.mismatch) and after B11's new map the client's host.recovered.newMap (owner, editor; B20 editors only); a refused creation -> host.status.notCreated 'No map was made yet.' with the reason row in the thumbnail slot; player's tab -> host.party.asOf 'As the party knows it, week {week}' (host.party.asOfUndated when week null) or host.party.notOpened 'The DM has not opened this map yet'; region label host.party.region 'Settlement map, as the party knows it'.

The frame draws everything else (@plat/app host mode, BCR-V8-3): map region, history panel (§4.6), report panel, gazetteer and 'features in view', item 101's tools by role, export menu by role and key, the tab's actions of §4.2 in the frame header (HostSlots.header; page operations post host.action), each shown only to the roles its row names. Host mode differs from the standalone app exactly (SR3-06): no file operations (New town, Open..., Save a copy, Recently deleted) and no permalink (V9 §2.2 fileMenu false; SR3-02: §11.1's permalinks need a DocResolver host mode does not configure); Settings without its Storage section (no local store, V9 §3.8 (6); J-V8.96); every action making a new document follows V9 §3.9's host-mode rule (newDocuments 'download'); the assistant as the host's clerk.config sets it (Assistant button only under builtin, else the card-only drawer for a host's proposal; V9 §2.2, §4.11; V10 §3.17) with no creation mode and no 'Start a new map from this'; history panel carries 'The party'; basic panel shows dossier-owned intent values (population, tier word) locked with reason 'Set by SettlementForge' (lockedControls, host.locked; §7.7 item 11) while port-derived map facts (wealth level, density) stay editable (§7.7 layer 1); only owner and editor frames exist; a co-DM frame has editor tools and exports by §11.1's key rules; header carries party controls; while 'See what the players see' is on a persistent strip 'Showing what the players see' with 'Show everything' (switches it off) stands for V9 §4.8's View-as banner while the host's party key is set (J-V8.89; X15); accessibility §14's; the iframe carries title 'Settlement map' and the map region its accessible name (one landmark).

Drawing the dossier's records (BCR-V8-15 adds §8.2 thematic and states rows, each with a program in ink, lit, hatched, falling back to the family's generic tint program): ConditionOverlay — drawn by its archetype's conditions row (siege: tint on the enceinte band and a hatched ring outside the wall; quarantine: desaturating tint over the built area and a barrier mark at every gate; occupation: a banner mark on the seat's building, new symbol occupation (§8.3); migration: item 70's camp clusters as the base draws them; others no mark); never labelled on the map, the cartouche legend names each drawn condition ('Under siege since week 40') for every key, an untinted archetype named only for a secret key (J-V8.40); GeoJSON one feature per overlay (kind condition, archetype, severity, weeks) without geometry, targets = addresses it tints; SVG/PNG tint groups under layer.thematic; persisted in the model. DepositSite — its land use as §4.9 draws it; depleted by states row worked-out (spoil heaps, stump field); removed nothing; labelled by the deposits row's label, a custom resource's name, or for a derived site its land use's label, as a hinterland feature label at the city band (§9.4); GeoJSON land-use feature gains deposit and depositState; model. PowerRelation — not drawn (item 72's political view reads it); JSON schema only; model. Dossier-backed Person — not drawn; gazetteer people list and the hover card of its workplace or home ('Works here: ...'); by its workplace's knowledge (withheld with the place; else public); people CSV and JSON schema; model. HistoryHint — nothing; JSON schema; the recipe.

Drawing custom content: CustomChainRecord — optional thematic view supplyChains (off by default): each ACTIVE chain as a dashed line along the way graph's shortest route between its placed nodes in flow order, an arrowhead at each node, endpoints drawn to their gate or quay; one colour per chain from the thematic palette in key order; inactive not drawn; Knowledge (SR-25; J-V8.103, .105): drawn, labelled, listed in the gazetteer and exported only when the key admits every joined node (the view's effective key for drawing, legend and gazetteer; the export's key for GeoJSON and pictures), each node binding a placed element admitted by its knownTo in §9.2's admission table as a band-less reader (as at the city band), a concealed use (item 63) never; otherwise not drawn, listed or exported; labelled in the view's legend and in the gazetteer under kind customChain (active only) — the read by which V9 §5.4 offers 'SettlementForge's chains' (XV-V9-26; host projection keeps the row); GeoJSON one LineString per admitted active chain on the view's route, kind supplyChain, key and label; SVG or PNG draws the view's chains under the same rule; model. CustomServiceRecord — not drawn (sub-location, item 104 (h)(5)); in its provider's hover card and the gazetteer; JSON schema; model.
